artworks.title: Diana and Actaeon
artworks.description: Titian's poesie for Philip II: Actaeon parts the curtain on Diana's bath at Gargaphie — the fatal glance that will turn the hunter into a stag.

artworks.title: The Death of Actaeon
artworks.description: The grim sequel: Actaeon already sprouting antlers collapses under his own hounds while Diana strides in with drawn bow — metamorphosis as late Titian storm.

artworks.title: The Transformation of Actaeon
artworks.description: Fontainebleau etching of Ovid's hinge: Diana sprinkles the hunter as antlers rise from his brow — the transformation that spreads the myth through print.

artworks.title: Apulian Red-figure Skyphos Depicting the Myth of Actaeon
artworks.description: South Italian skyphos in Karlsruhe: Actaeon set upon by his hounds as Artemis enacts his destruction — the myth on painted clay long before Titian.

popCulture.title: Diana and Actaeon
popCulture.creator: Titian
popCulture.description: Titian's poesie for Philip II freezes the fatal glance — Artemis' bath as the modern West's image of Actaeon's doom.

popCulture.title: Actaeon
popCulture.description: The hunter torn by his own hounds remains Ovid's caution against seeing what gods keep private.
